eyebrow: SQL Server Performance Tuning · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 16 · Index Tuning in Depth

code:
Rowstore (every index so far)
  each ROW's columns stored together
  great for finding a few specific rows

Columnstore
  each COLUMN stored together, compressed
  great for scanning millions of rows,
  touching only a few columns

SELECT ProductCategory, SUM(SalesAmount)
FROM dbo.FactSales GROUP BY ProductCategory;
caption: Different shape, different job entirely.

code:
Compression
  same-typed column values together
  compress far better than mixed rows

Batch mode execution
  ~900 rows processed per batch
  not one row at a time

Both advantages VANISH for a
single-row point lookup by key.
caption: Built for aggregates over huge tables — not OLTP lookups.

code:
-- Becomes the table's primary storage
CREATE CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX CCI_FactSales
    ON dbo.FactSales;

-- An analytical copy alongside a rowstore table
CREATE NONCLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX
    NCCI_FactSales_Analytics
    ON dbo.FactSales
       (ProductCategory, SalesAmount,
        Quantity, OrderDateKey);
caption: Clustered replaces storage; nonclustered sits alongside it.
